scope: mix check from fresh clones of committed sources, including the Hex archive and out-of-tree compilation gate, on both required Elixir/OTP runtimes

source_identity.kind: git clone --no-local of each committed HEAD inside the container; no working-tree copy

environment.platform: Linux arm64 (Docker Desktop VM on macOS arm64)
environment.container: docker run --rm --init --cpus 4 --memory 6g with read-only source mounts; the check runs as unprivileged uid 1000 so permission-denial tests observe ordinary filesystem semantics
commands: git clone --no-local SOURCE /work/src/REPOSITORY for wotex, wotex-runtime and wotex-coap

assertions: Both lanes clone committed HEADs and pass every configured mix check tool with exit 0
The archive tool builds the Hex package, checks its outer and packaged contents, development-artifact exclusion and dependency identities, and compiles it out of tree on both runtimes
Both runtimes produce the byte-identical Hex archive
The application-free tool confirms no Application callback and that starting the application and constructing PSK and PKI security values starts no SSL supervisor, on both runtimes
The cloned working trees stay clean after the full check

defects_found.observed: Dialyzer on OTP 27 reported an opaque ets:tid type test and a contract supertype for Native.Body.new/0
A fixture helper wrote two open replies back to back; coalesced in one read they failed start instead of closing after it
After a lost Port handle the fixture helper, an Elixir script, stopped gracefully on SIGTERM too slowly for the cleanup bound on OTP 27
Coverage was 94.9% on OTP 27 against the 95% floor
defects_found.fixed_by: 6edd61b adds tests for encoder, workspace and build-verification edges

defects_found.observed: Running the check as root let the unreadable-artifact test read a mode-0 file
defects_found.fixed_by: the lane runs as an unprivileged user

unaccepted: The macOS-arm64 clean clone check; macOS runs the same gate from the working tree
Hex dependency resolution without WOTEX_PATH_DEPS, which awaits published core and Runtime packages
